title: Item Recovery in Microsoft Fabric (Generally Available)
summary: A Fabric Updates Blog post announcing General Availability of Item Recovery, a tenant-configurable safety net that moves deleted Fabric items into a soft-deleted, restorable state instead of removing them immediately. It covers how the Workspace Recycle bin and REST API restore items, how the retention window is configured, and how admins should roll it into runbooks and governance tooling.
audience: Fabric tenant admins, workspace admins, and support/on-call engineers responsible for recovering accidentally deleted workspace items.
why_it_matters: Accidental deletion has historically been an unrecoverable, high-severity incident in Fabric; a governed, admin-controlled recovery window changes operational runbooks and reduces the blast radius of user error, which matters for any capacity/governance design guidance.
takeaways: Item Recovery reached General Availability effective June 30, 2026, moving beyond its prior Preview state.
Deleted supported items go through a soft-delete + retention window rather than immediate permanent deletion.
Retention windows are configurable up to 90 days and adjustable by tenant admins at any time.
Recovery is available both through the Workspace Recycle bin UI and via REST API, enabling automation.
Coverage is scoped to the item types already supported in Preview, with more workloads planned over time.

claims.text: Item Recovery in Microsoft Fabric reached General Availability effective June 30, 2026, having previously been available in Preview.

When a supported item is deleted, it moves to a soft-deleted state rather than being removed immediately, and its content, metadata, and permissions remain intact and restorable during the retention window.
Deleted items can be restored either through the Workspace Recycle bin in the portal UI or programmatically via a REST API.
Tenant admins can configure a retention window of up to 90 days for Item Recovery and can adjust that window at any time.
After the configured retention window expires, a soft-deleted item is permanently deleted and can no longer be restored.
At GA, Item Recovery covers the same set of item types that were already supported during the Preview phase, with Microsoft stating it is actively working to extend coverage to more workloads.

The GA guidance recommends that tenant admins review and confirm the Item Recovery tenant setting under Fabric admin portal > Tenant settings against organizational policy as an operational rollout step.
Organizations using automation for audit or compliance are advised to evaluate integrating Item Recovery's REST APIs and audit events into existing governance workflows.
